implementation_notes:
# Four-cycle restoring divider

The bench core scored **69.24 CoreMark iterations/s**, up from 12.12. Median Gowin Fmax rose from 5.442 MHz to **31.097 MHz**. Ten iterations took **4,491,485 bracketed cycles**, matching the supplied baseline.

| Gowin placement option | Fmax (MHz) |
| --- | ---: |
| 0 | 30.723 |
| 1 | 31.097 |
| 2 | 31.097 |

The divider captures the forwarded operand magnitudes on issue. Each of the next four clocks computes eight quotient bits through a shared chain of trial subtractions. The final quotient or remainder is selected and sign-corrected from registers and held until EX/MEM accepts it. A zero divisor naturally produces an all-ones quotient and the dividend magnitude as remainder. The issue logic suppresses quotient negation in that case. The same magnitude arithmetic gives the specified signed overflow result for INT_MIN divided by −1.

EX also saves the original forwarded operands for channel-0 RVFI. A stalled memory request holds EX/MEM and delays issue. Once it advances, EX writes bubbles with zero controls while the divider runs. The PC and ID/EX can advance on the result-transfer edge, allowing an immediate consumer to use the existing EX/MEM forwarding path. The ALTOPS implementation captures the specified formula at issue and uses the same completion handshake.

The four arithmetic clocks are between a separate issue edge and a result-transfer edge. With memory ready, a divide therefore occupies EX for six clocks. This latency matters for workloads with divisions inside the measured interval. The longest path on placement option 0 runs between quotient registers through the eight trial subtractions. Gowin reported a 37.843 ns arrival time, 2,852 logic cells and 562 registers for that placement.

## Local verification

- Verilator passed the requested wildcard lint command with zero warnings.
- The ALTOPS formal suite passed all 53 checks on the first run.
- All 81 cocotb tests passed. The divider tests cover every divisor width, signed overflow, divide by zero, consecutive operations, exact result latency and stability under delayed acceptance. Pipeline tests compare RVFI operands and results and count accepted memory transactions across load stalls.
- Cosimulation passed for selftest and three random instruction programs with and without bus stalls. CoreMark passed with both buses stalled pseudo-randomly, all five canonical CRCs, the validation message and zero out-of-bounds accesses. Its start and stop markers were at cycles 15,801 and 4,507,286.
lesson: - 2026-11-22 hyp-20261122-001-r1s0 (regression, +471.29%): Folding combinational DIV/REM into four steps of eight quotient bits shortened the EX critical path and raised median Gowin Fmax from 5.442 to 31.097 MHz, while timed cycles stayed flat because CoreMark executes all five DIVU sites outside its timing markers.

title: Fold DIV and REM into a four-round execute unit
motivation: Gowin reports a 199.837 ns, 156-cell path through operand forwarding and the EX ALU. The baseline puts full-width signed and unsigned division and remainder in the ALU result mux. These operators are the most likely source of its depth. A reference-interpreter run of the canonical 2K, -O3, ten-iteration ELF matched all five CRCs. Of 2,922,015 instructions retired between the marker writes, 93,960 were MUL and zero were DIV, DIVU, REM or REMU.

Replace the four combinational DIV/REM operations with one blocking restoring divider. Capture forwarded operands and their signs on issue. Compute eight quotient bits per clock for four clocks, registering the quotient and partial remainder after each round. Select and sign-correct the result on transfer to EX/MEM. The instruction counts predict zero divider wait cycles in the measured interval. Check the cycle count and median Fmax separately. The multiplier and the eight-step divider round are candidates for the new longest path.

title: Predict the next fetch PC from decode-stage register values
motivation:
The baseline fetches PC+4 after every instruction. IF and ID share a cycle,
so each aligned taken branch or jump squashes one fetch slot when EX redirects.
Both source registers are already read in that cycle, including same-cycle WB
bypass. When these values are current, they give the exact branch direction
or indirect jump target. Restricting prediction to those signals keeps the
predictor off the combinational EX ALU result path.

A scratch RTL prototype ran the ten-iteration CoreMark timing bracket in
4,163,829 cycles with both stall generators active, down from 4,491,485.
All five CRCs matched. Gowin reported 5.128, 5.447 and 5.447 MHz across its
three placement options. The median gives 13.08 iterations/s, 7.9% above
the 12.12 baseline, at a cost of 471 additional LUT4s. The prototype passed
all 53 single-retire ALTOPS formal checks.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict the successor of each accepted instruction in the combined IF/ID
stage. For a legal conditional branch, evaluate its funct3 comparison on
the two current register-file read values. Predict the PC-relative target
on true and PC+4 on false. For JAL use the J target, and for legal JALR
use (rs1_read + I-immediate) with bit zero cleared. Select the target only
if it is word-aligned and below 0x00100000. Otherwise predict PC+4.
A pending register write can make a prediction stale, so EX resolves every
transfer using its forwarded operands, alignment checks and trap rules.

When a valid control transfer advances through EX, compare its resolved
successor against the current registered fetch PC. That PC is the prediction
selected at the edge that admitted this instruction to ID/EX. A mismatch
redirects to the resolved successor and kills the younger instruction.
A match lets ID accept the current fetch without a control bubble. Hold
both the PC and ID/EX during a data-memory freeze. On release, correction
takes priority even when imemReady is low. A load-use bubble or unready
instruction bus must never consume a prediction. EX supplies the resolved
pc_next to RVFI and PC+4 as the jump link value.

title: Shorten the divider feedback path to five quotient bits per clock
motivation:
The champion's worst reported Gowin path starts and ends at remainder_q[1].
It crosses eight dependent trial subtractions in one clock and has a
reported arrival time of 37.434 ns. The prior CoreMark trace retired zero
DIV or REM instructions inside the timing markers, so spending three extra
clocks per divide should buy Fmax at little cost to measured cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Run the existing restoring divider for seven rounds of five quotient bits.
Load a 35-bit shift register with three leading zeros and the 32-bit
dividend magnitude. Each round consumes five bits from the top, appends
five quotient bits at the bottom and registers the partial remainder.
After 35 steps the low 32 quotient bits and the remainder give the RV32M
results. This cuts the chain of subtract-and-select decisions from eight
to five while retaining the divider's current request and response ports.

the three Gowin placement options. The worst paths now end at the ID/EX
operand registers. Stalled CoreMark passed CRC validation and used
4,491,485 marker cycles for ten iterations, matching the champion.
The 43.681 MHz median therefore gives 97.25 iterations/s, up 37.1%
from 70.94. The three extra clocks apply to each DIV/REM on workloads
that use these instructions.

title: Shorten the divider feedback path with parallel radix-4 digit selection
motivation:
Gowin traces the champion's 37.434 ns worst path from the divider's remainder
register back to itself. Each clock crosses eight dependent trial subtractions
and remainder selections. The prior CoreMark trace counted zero DIV or REM
instructions between the markers. A shorter feedback path can therefore raise
Fmax with negligible cost to the measured 4,491,485 cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the binary restoring round with three radix-4 digit selections per
clock. For each digit, bring down two dividend bits and subtract D, 2D and 3D

subtract/select depth from eight to three at the cost of two more parallel
subtractors per digit and three additional clocks per division.

At the champion's marker cycle count, 41.4 MHz would yield about 92.2
iterations/s, a 30% gain. The acceptance threshold is about 33.33 MHz at
that cycle count. Check the post-route median and marker cycles separately.
Routing the parallel trials or the existing single-cycle multiply could
set the new clock limit.

title: Predict recurring control transfers with a 128-entry branch target buffer
motivation:
The champion fetches PC+4 and loses one fetch slot on each taken transfer.
Its timed CoreMark trace has about 358,000 taken branches and jumps in ten
iterations. The previous decode-operand predictor saved 7.3% of cycles.
A branch target buffer (BTB) can recover most of those slots by reading
the last resolved target and a direction counter directly from the fetch PC.

A scratch prototype on the champion's four-round divider core ran the same
ten iterations in 4,190,005 bracketed cycles, down from 4,491,485 with
both bus stall generators enabled. All five CRCs matched. The three Gowin
placements reached 31.291, 32.104 and 32.104 MHz. The median gives
76.62 iterations/s, 8.0% above the 70.94 champion. At this cycle count
the acceptance threshold requires a median above 31.0912 MHz. The worst
path for placement 0 still ran through the divider. That placement used
2,987 LUT4s, 565 registers and seven block RAMs. The prototype passed
all 53 single-retire ALTOPS formal checks. A directed test confirmed
consecutive retirements for a trained loop branch and its target.

Widen t before shifting. The disjoint fields let the first sum use wiring.
Only the low-part product needs a multiplier, and both factors fit in
16 bits. R equals N - q*D and is less than D. For s=1, q*Dlo <= 65535.
For the other shifts D >= 2^(16+s/2), q < 2^(16-s/2) and Dlo < 2^s,
so q*Dlo < D. Thus R > -D. A negative R needs exactly one decrement of
q and one addition of D to R. This yields exact DIV and REM for every
divisor in the large class.

register the scaled operands, the next round to form the multiples, four
rounds for quotient digits and the sixth round to register the low-part
product and concatenated remainder. In the response cycle form R and its
borrow. Capture these and q at the EX/MEM edge. Give the trial array its
own registered d for the 1d, 2d, 4d and 8d inputs. Use a separate setup
operand mux to form the odd multiples so phase selection stays off the
remainder feedback path. Sample request operands while the unit is idle.

signed correction term from D for a remainder, or from -1 for a quotient,

negate bit, add the correction term only on borrow, and use negate as

Compute DIV/REM with a synchronous coefficient ROM and registered DSP
products. Latch the raw operands and sign flags at request. Form unsigned
magnitudes N and D on the setup edge. For D >= 2 set s = max(0, floor(log2(D))-8).
Determine s alongside magnitude formation. If B is the divisor bits XOR
its replicated negate flag, D reaches 2^i when any B[31:i] bit is set
or when negation increments an all-ones B[i-1:0]. Index the ROM with
k = D >> s and let u be the first eight fractional bits of D / 2^s.

Use T = 2^34. Store A[k] = ceil(T/k), H[k] = A[k]-A[k+1], and
C[k] = floor(T/(k*(k+1)^2)). Store zero H and C for k < 256 where
u is always zero. Include A[512] when computing the last slope.
The row widths are 34, 18 and 10 bits. Read p = u*(256-u) alongside
the coefficients. Register H*u and C*p in parallel, then register
M = A - ((H*u) >> 8) - ((C*p) >> 16). All ROM entries are elaboration
constants. Compute q = ((N*M) >> 34) >> s from a full 66-bit product,
then form P = q*D, retaining 33 bits.

The interpolation is an upper bound. At x=u/256, the excess of the
unrounded secant over 1/(k+x) is x*(1-x)/(k*(k+1)*(k+x)).
Subtracting x*(1-x)/(k*(k+1)^2) leaves at most (4/27)/k^4.
At s >= 1, k >= 256, this adds less than 0.075 to N/D. The table
and product roundings add less than 3.25*N/(T*2^s). Truncating x
costs less than N/(256*2^s*k^2) and is exact through s=8. The sum
stays below one, including s >= 9 where the fraction term is below
0.5. At s=0 only the endpoint rounding applies. Hence q is exact or
one too large and P fits in 33 bits.

interpolation products, M, N*M, shifted quotient, and P. At response

base (low R for REM, q for DIV), XORed with the replicated output sign,
plus the borrow and a precomputed correction term. The unsigned term
is D for REM or -1 for DIV. Reverse the term for a negative result.
